item.title: Toba Aquarium: Home of Japan's Only Dugong — Guide
item.description: Toba Aquarium, on the pearl-fishing coast of Toba, is one of Japan’s largest and most beloved aquariums, home to around 1,200 species — one of the highest counts in the country — displayed across twelve themed zones with no fixed route, so visitors wander freely. Its greatest celebrity is Serena, the only dugong on public display anywhere in Japan, joined by playful sea otters, capybaras, rare finless porpoises and a giant spider-crab tank.

item.title: Izu Peninsula Scuba Diving: Japan's Favourite Dive Coast — Guide
item.description: The Izu Peninsula is mainland Japan’s most popular scuba diving region, its volcanic underwater terrain washed by the warm Kuroshio Current, which carries subtropical fish and nurtures soft coral gardens surprisingly close to Tokyo. Famous sites include Osezaki on the west coast, whose sheltered bay suits beginners and training while its outer wall drops steeply into Suruga Bay’s depths, and the east coast’s rocky points, with dive shops in the seaside towns running guided boat and shore dives year-round.

item.title: Oarai Aquarium: One of Japan's Largest Shark Collections — Guide
item.description: Aqua World Oarai, the aquarium at Oarai, displays roughly 580 species of marine life across its exhibits, with a particular focus that has made it one of Japan’s leading facilities for shark and ocean sunfish (mola mola) displays. Large tanks recreate the Pacific and Kashima-nada ecosystems found just offshore, and the aquarium’s oceanfront location, a short distance from the iconic Oarai torii gate, makes it easy to combine with the area’s other coastal sights.
